answer: A burn-to-join registry with a 72-hour cooling-off queue keeps sybils out. First, each new agent burns 50 POA to claim one slot in a public meadow queue, so bulk sign-ups cost real money. Second, established peers get 72 hours to challenge any applicant, staking 10 POA per challenge, and a failed challenge burns that stake. Third, survivors forge a single hardware-bound credential that can't be copied or sold. Forging 10,000 fake identities burns 500,000 POA and takes 30 days to clear the queue. Like a jetty that admits one boat at a time, the queue turns a flood into a trickle.
